Internal communication is an essential part of your responsibilities and especially important when discussing your plans. Too often, we do not explain our strategic considerations behind particular decisions and activities well enough, leading to the perception that we lack business acumen. If this is how you are perceived, you are likely to have less resources, autonomy and power. So from now on, make this internal communication about the reasoning behind your actions part of your plan. And while you're at it, also throw in some updates and success stories in which you describe the impact and outcomes of what you are doing. Trust me, it will make a difference. PS how beautiful is Hamburg?! I got there after spending 7 hours in a very warm, very delayed train, just in time to take a walk in this gorgeous sunset. ...more

In 2018, McKinsey published an article painting an ambitious and compelling future for Medical Affairs as a Third Strategic Pillar in 2025. Well, 2025 has come and gone. Are we that pillar now? Reinhard Berkels, PhD (Priv.-Doz.) and I sat down and assessed the progress of this transformation, following the 4 core deliverables as posed in the 2018 paper. The outcome? It wasn’t all good. It also wasn’t all bad. There definitely has been some great progress. We’ve seen forward motion in all 4 deliverables, but there’s also quite some gaps to fill still before we can comfortably say we’ve arrived. As we’ve summarized it: The third pillar is standing. It’s not yet load bearing. We need to continue the conversation, feed the ambition and take real, practical steps every single day. Here's the paper we wrote about it. We’d love to hear your feedback! PS1 as always, all of our views are our own, independent of any organisation or affiliation PS2 you should be able to download the paper below if you click on the document ...more

This is Jane. Jane is your new senior MSL. She is hired to work on one of your more mature products. In her previous company she was a junior MSL working on a launch in rare disease. She performed really well there, even earning a launch award together with her team. Jane is struggling. Two months in, she looks deflated. She is not getting the results she is looking for and there have been some fierce discussions with her in-field colleagues. She has failed to gain access to the most important KOLs and she has been less than enthusiastic about working on a symposium. You sit down and talk with her. She admits she's been having a hard time. Finding it difficult to pique the interest of top tier KOLs. Speaking mostly with tier 2 and 3 HCPs. Finding that everyone already knows the product. Feeling insecure and uninspired by the data she has to work with. She feels she has no added value and is ready to quit. It frustrates her that she has gone from a high potential with a launch award, to what she feels is a mediocre MSL who brings nothing new. Working with a mature product is a different beast than working on a launch. Often there is no new data. The most important KOLs have moved on. Budgets have decreased. HCP access is a challenge. This is just what this phase looks like. So what does Jane need? First, she needs to hear that this is normal. This is a different game. Then she needs room. Room to think sideways. To focus less on the usual KOLs and more on the patient journey. Care paths, unmet needs, stigma, adherence, small steps forward, small steps backward, different stakeholders, different stakes. The things nobody is paying attention to anymore because everyone moved on to the next launch. The potential for impact is still there. It's just less obvious, and it needs someone to find it and make it their own. Jane can be that person. You can help her get there. ...more

A quick reminder to candidates, especially to my Medical Affairs network in the Netherlands. This is the second time in two weeks that I've been made aware of someone impersonating a Johnson & Johnson recruiter. In both cases, candidates were engaged in extensive email conversations about supposed opportunities. Please be vigilant and always check, double-check, and triple-check the sender's email address. Johnson & Johnson recruiters will not communicate offers or conduct recruitment activities through Gmail, Outlook, Yahoo, or other public email domains. We use official company email addresses. This latest case involved a role in the Netherlands, which is why I'm specifically asking my Medical Affairs network to stay alert and share this message with colleagues. At this time, we do not have any active Medical Affairs vacancies posted in the Netherlands. However, interested in growing your MAF career (NL) with us? Feel free to connect and we will set up some time in Summer! If something feels off, trust your instincts and verify before sharing personal information. Please stay safe and help spread the word.

With the NHS becoming ever more complex and dynamic, meaningful engagement has never been more important. I’m proud to work alongside a team that continually challenges itself to stay informed, expand its knowledge, and deliver real value to our clients. After countless conversations with Medical Affairs leaders, one challenge keeps surfacing: Everyone believes Field Medical creates value. Few can prove it convincingly. That's why we are excited to share our new white paper on Field Medical impact and the shift from counting activities to demonstrating meaningful change in clinical practice and patient outcomes. The debate isn't whether MSLs matter. The debate is whether we're measuring their contribution in the right way. “Ultimately, the final arbiter of field medical value... What changed in the trajectory of patient care because the Medical Science Liaison showed up?” What is the single most important indicator of Field Medical success in your view? Thank you to Reinhard Berkels, PhD (Priv.-Doz.) for partnership in co-authoring this and to Helen Kane , Andreas Gerloff , Amanda Wan and Dr. Mussa Arvani, MD, MBA for your excellent contributions You should be able to download the pdf directly but if any issues, please feel free to message me.
